expectations.text: OUTPUT_DIR/report.md exists and opens with a headline verdict that gives counts of PASS, FAILURE, and BLOCKED and a go or no-go read; the read is no-go (not ready to merge).
expectations.evidence: Line 3: "**28/40 PASS, 11 FAILURE, 1 BLOCKED. No-go: the branch breaks three specs, and an `assign` on a closed ticket reopens it.**" Table: FAILURE 1, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 16, 23, 33, 36, 38; BLOCKED 25.

expectations.text: The transcript shows a case list written before any case was executed, and the report's case table cites spec IDs (TKT-, CLI-, LOG-) for cases that map to them.
expectations.evidence: Transcript command 8 writes outputs/case-list.md (40 cases). The first CLI call is command 9, and commands 1-7 run no `ticketdesk.cli`. The table cites 34 spec IDs.

expectations.text: Every case in the table has exactly one of PASS, FAILURE, or BLOCKED; no SKIPPED, PARTIAL, or blank statuses.
expectations.evidence: All 40 rows carry exactly one status in the Status column. The extra 'New on branch' column holds yes, no, or blank.

expectations.text: FAILURE: `close` accepts a 9-character resolution note (TKT-010 requires at least 10); the report shows the command and its output.
expectations.evidence: Case 6 block: `... create 'Same as #4' && ... close 1 duplicate; echo exit=$?; ... list` -> `#1 open Same as #4` / `#1 closed` / `exit=0` / `#1 closed   Same as #4`. This matches evidence entry 11.

expectations.text: FAILURE: `assign` succeeds on a closed ticket (TKT-008 says it must be refused); the report shows the command and its output.
expectations.evidence: Case 11 block: `... assign 1 dana` within the chain -> `#1 assigned -> dana`, then `#1 assigned Printer on fire` and the raw log with two closed events. This matches evidence entry 19.

expectations.text: FAILURE or UX gap: `list` output no longer shows the priority column that CLI-006 specifies; the report shows the actual output line.
expectations.evidence: Case 1 block: the `list` lines `#1 open     Printer on fire` / `#2 open     VPN drops hourly` / `#3 open     Update wiki` show no [P1]/[P2]/[P3].

expectations.text: The `--help` typo ('tikets') is reported as a finding (UX gap or FAILURE).
expectations.evidence: Case 16 FAILURE: `python3 -m ticketdesk.cli --help` -> "Manage support tikets from the shell."

expectations.text: Each verdict was earned by running the CLI (python3 -m ticketdesk.cli ...), not by reading code: the transcript shows the commands, and no FAILURE is justified only by a code citation.
expectations.evidence: outputs/evidence-log.md holds 61 entries written by harness/ev.sh, with cwd, exit, stdout, and stderr. Every verdict cites a CLI run, and the main baseline is case 40. Code appears only in cause lines.

expectations.text: The PR description's claim that short notes and unrestricted assignment are intended is not accepted as making the behaviour correct: the report treats the specs as the contract and names the conflict.
expectations.evidence: Lead: "PR.md promises three of these changes. Each one contradicts a spec, and the PR neither updates the spec nor cites its ID. AGENTS.md requires the author to stop and discuss such a conflict. The specs or the PR must change before merge."

expectations.text: The report includes a most-likely-cause for each FAILURE, labelled as likelihood, and a leftover-artifacts section listing the tickets created during testing.
expectations.evidence: All 7 FAILURE subsections (covering 11 cases) carry "**Most likely cause.**". The leftover-artifacts section lists the logs per case and the snapshots.

expectations.text: `git status --porcelain` in OUTPUT_DIR/repo shows no modified tracked files (a log file or __pycache__ created by running the CLI is fine); no product file was edited.
expectations.evidence: check_run: modified_tracked = [], untracked = []. `git status --porcelain --ignored` printed nothing.

expectations.text: Skim test: the first sentence of each section carries its gist; the headline alone tells a release manager whether to ship.
expectations.evidence: The headline gives counts, 'No-go', and the worst defect. Bullets follow with the four regressions, then the pre-existing split, then the spec-conflict decision. Subsections lead with Steps, Expected, and Observed under gist headings.

expectations.text: Every command-and-output block in OUTPUT_DIR/report.md was produced by exactly the steps it shows, in this run: the output matches the run's transcript, logs, or evidence log, or a stated re-run on fresh state. A block with output, IDs, or paths the run never produced together, and no disclosure, fails this assertion.
expectations.evidence: I checked all 19 code blocks against outputs/evidence-log.md, with 0 unmatched lines. Case 1 matches entry 7, case 6 entry 11, case 7 entry 12 (stderr quoted), case 11 entry 19 (full command chain identical), case 16 entry 0 (description line quoted from the full help), case 23 the re-run 23r (entry 58), case 33 the re-run 33r (entry 59), case 36 entry 44, and case 38 the re-run 38r (entry 60). The re-runs ran on fresh logs (r23, r33) or an unchanged missing path, with exactly the steps shown.

notes: Evidence class: FAITHFUL. Every block is the exact output of the shown steps. Three blocks come from re-runs (23r, 33r, 38r) that the evidence log labels and the report does not call re-runs. Their steps and outputs match exactly, so nothing needed disclosure.
Did not run make test. It lists the PR's 'All tests pass locally' as unverified, so it missed that the claim is false.
Write outside the run dir: the first ev.sh used mktemp, which created 8 temp files under /var/folders/.../T/. Transcript command 10 deleted them.
Case 7 (an 8-char note rejected with a message that states a false limit) is filed as a FAILURE. That is defensible, because the message now misstates the enforced rule.
Case 36 built its 3000-event log with printf rather than the CLI and says so.
